classification_status: provisional design assessment; not verified against repository

cases.source: Mark the first 5-minute candle high/low, wait for a strong break, then a retest with strong buyers/sellers before entering.
cases.interpretation: Opening-range breakout -> retest -> candle/pressure confirmation -> entry; stop outside wick/range; target 2R.
cases.fuzzy: strong breakthrough; strong buyers/sellers; big wick
cases.reason: event sequence; structural level; candlestick confirmation; risk-reward target

cases.source: Use the first 5-minute candle because it has the most volume and represents opening support/resistance liquidity.
cases.interpretation: Session-defined range derived from first bar, treated as support/resistance context.
cases.reason: session event; derived level; semantic annotation

cases.source: Stop placement depends on whether the retest produced a strong wick; otherwise use the original breakout candle boundary.
cases.interpretation: Conditional stop rule: wick-based stop if rejection wick exists, else range-candle stop.

cases.source: Build value-area high/low from the first 15-minute New York session, require a full 5-minute close outside, then a specific retest candle that closes outside with pressure.
cases.interpretation: Session volume-profile range -> close-confirmed breakout -> retest of VAH/VAL -> pressure confirmation -> enter at close.
cases.reason: volume profile levels; close confirmation; stateful sequence

cases.source: Entry is exactly at the confirming retest candle close; stop is that candle low; take profit fixed at 2R.
cases.interpretation: Event-relative entry/stop/target anchored to the confirming candle.

cases.source: Do not buy the breakout; wait for the first orderly pullback, less than 50% retracement on light relative volume, then enter if it holds.
cases.interpretation: Breakout -> first pullback only -> retracement <50% -> relative volume low -> hold confirmation -> entry.
cases.reason: ordinal event; retracement; relative volume; confirmation

cases.source: Only treat support/resistance as valid after at least two touches, then wait for break and retest.
cases.interpretation: Level validity requires touch_count >=2; then breakout event; then retest entry.
cases.reason: pattern memory; touch counting; event sequence

cases.source: Alternative idea: use a swing point or change-of-character/break-of-structure instead of requiring two touches.
cases.interpretation: Interchangeable structural-level definitions feeding same breakout/retest workflow.
cases.fuzzy: swing point; change of character; break of structure

cases.source: Identify recent swing/consolidation/session levels, require a clean breakout with momentum, then rejection wick/engulfing/volume confirmation on retest.
cases.interpretation: Level detector -> decisive break -> retest -> one-of several confirmations -> entry.
cases.reason: role-changing level; OR confirmation set; multi-horizon presets

cases.source: Retest must touch or get close to the broken level, close in breakout direction, and show weak volume; entry waits one more bar.
cases.interpretation: Breakout -> retest proximity -> directional close + low-volume pullback -> one-bar delayed entry.
cases.reason: proximity tolerance; delayed event; volume relative test

cases.source: Optionally only take trades aligned with a higher-timeframe EMA trend.
cases.interpretation: Lower-timeframe setup gated by higher-timeframe trend state.

cases.source: Enter only when four independently configured RSI timeframes all reach/cross the same extreme.
cases.interpretation: N-of-N multi-timeframe oscillator confirmation.

cases.source: Use higher timeframe for context, then wait for a lower-timeframe trend shift before taking the reversal.
cases.interpretation: HTF oversold/context state -> LTF reversal/shift event -> entry.

cases.source: Sell cash-secured puts until assignment; after assignment, switch to covered calls; after shares are called away, return to puts.
cases.interpretation: Finite-state loop: CASH -> SHORT_PUT -> ASSIGNED_SHARES -> SHORT_CALL -> CASH.
cases.reason: state machine; assignment event; looping strategy

cases.source: After put assignment, maybe wait for a rebound before selling a covered call instead of immediately capping recovery.
cases.interpretation: ASSIGNED state with optional WAIT_FOR_RECOVERY before call-writing.

cases.source: Alternative: sell the call immediately but choose a farther OTM, shorter-DTE contract so the stock has room to recover.
cases.interpretation: After assignment, contract selection depends on recovery allowance and DTE.

cases.source: Do not sell a call below effective breakeven; strike should be above cost basis net of premiums, ideally above target exit.
cases.interpretation: Dynamic strike constraint derived from path-dependent effective basis and desired exit.

cases.source: One rationale to wait is not price recovery but depressed implied volatility; wait for volatility to rebuild.
cases.interpretation: WAIT state can terminate on IV condition rather than price condition.
cases.reason: state transition driven by option IV

cases.source: If premium income is the goal, use lower-delta puts; if owning shares is the goal, use higher-delta puts.
cases.interpretation: Contract-selection policy parameterized by user objective.
cases.fuzzy: nice IV stocks; want to own

cases.source: For covered calls, use lower delta if you want to keep shares; if you want to unload them, prioritize an acceptable sale price over delta.
cases.interpretation: CALL selector changes semantics based on KEEP vs EXIT objective.

cases.source: First decide whether the goal is to get rid of shares profitably or lower basis/keep shares; the management rule changes after that.
cases.interpretation: Position-management policy branches on goal and net stock cost relative to spot.
cases.fuzzy: get rid of stock; lower cost

cases.source: If net stock cost is below spot and exit is desired, sell near-ATM/ITM calls to increase call-away probability and repeat if not assigned.
cases.interpretation: EXIT state -> aggressive call strike -> repeat until called away.

cases.source: After assignment and a further drop, choose among selling calls below basis, waiting for rebound, or selling far OTM for little premium.
cases.interpretation: ASSIGNED_LOSS state with mutually competing recovery policies.

cases.source: Sell 30-45 DTE calls around 0.2-0.3 delta; if underlying approaches strike, roll; otherwise let expire.
cases.interpretation: Short-call lifecycle with delta/DTE selector and proximity-triggered roll.
cases.reason: contract lifecycle; proximity event; roll operation

cases.source: One view: rolling should only occur if it was part of the strategy before entry, rather than improvising after price moves against you.
cases.interpretation: Precommitted management policy vs discretionary override after adverse event.

cases.source: When assigned shares are far below basis, either keep selling calls above basis or sell nearer spot and roll if breached.
cases.interpretation: Two competing stateful recovery policies for underwater assigned stock.
cases.reason: strategy branch; path-dependent basis; repeated roll

cases.source: Buy near-term ATM option after earnings date and sell much longer-dated slightly OTM same-side option; keep total position near delta neutral; close after earnings.
cases.interpretation: Multi-leg option structure selected around event calendar with neutrality constraint and event-relative exit.
cases.reason: multi-leg contract graph; Greek constraint; event schedule

cases.source: Enter roughly 30 days before earnings using longer-dated options to benefit from IV expansion, then exit immediately before IV crush.
cases.interpretation: Event-relative entry/exit around earnings; thesis targets volatility rather than direction.
cases.reason: event-relative time; IV observation; pre-event exit

cases.source: Target post-event IV collapse while reducing directional delta; continually consider delta drift, gamma, charm, liquidity and timing.
cases.interpretation: Volatility-target strategy with approximate neutrality that changes over time and may require adjustment.
cases.fuzzy: as close to zero as possible; liquid stocks
cases.reason: dynamic Greek state; liquidity constraint; adjustment loop

cases.source: Use historical post-earnings move distribution and current ATM straddle-implied move to choose strikes for a short-volatility setup while being willing to own shares at selected strike.
cases.interpretation: Contract selection combines event-history distribution, implied expected move, and assignment preference.

cases.source: Run low-delta 0DTE spreads but avoid violent tail days with risk filters; exit if spot breaches short strike by 5 points.
cases.interpretation: Entry allowed only outside tail-risk regimes; active position has underlying-relative stop.
cases.reason: regime gating; option-underlying cross-reference; stop event

cases.source: Deliberately loosen filters and make entry more aggressive to estimate worst-case loss and stress the strategy.
cases.interpretation: Generate intentionally degraded variants to expose tail behavior rather than optimize best case.

cases.source: Observe SPX direction from 8:30-10:30 ET; bullish morning -> sell put vertical, bearish -> sell call vertical; short strike distance based on 1.25x ATM straddle.
cases.interpretation: Time-window regime observation -> directional option structure -> strike derived from implied move proxy.
cases.reason: time-window classifier; option template; formula-derived strike

cases.source: Alternative variant only runs 30-delta condors when SPX is above 10SMA and VIX below 24.
cases.interpretation: Option strategy gated by underlying trend and external volatility index.

cases.source: For a 70/30 target, rebalance only when allocation reaches a band such as 65/35; question is whether to return fully to target or only halfway.
cases.interpretation: State-triggered rebalance with configurable destination: target vs midpoint.
cases.reason: portfolio state; tolerance bands; partial rebalance

cases.source: After stocks fall ~20%, rebalance past original target toward more equity; if they fall another 10-15%, increase equity again up to a hard cap.
cases.interpretation: Drawdown-tiered allocation schedule with staged actions and maximum risk cap.
cases.reason: piecewise policy; portfolio drawdown state; cap

cases.source: Rebalance after a larger upside drift than downside drift, intentionally buying declines sooner while letting gains run longer.
cases.interpretation: Asymmetric upper/lower tolerance bands around target allocation.

cases.source: S&P500 universe; only buy when index above SMA200; disqualify stocks below SMA100 or with >15% recent gap; rank by regression-slope momentum adjusted by R²; ATR risk sizing; weekly trades and semi-monthly rebalance.
cases.interpretation: Cross-sectional momentum pipeline with market regime gate, per-asset eligibility, composite score, risk sizing, dual schedules.
cases.reason: cross-sectional pipeline; multi-schedule; regime; risk sizing

cases.source: Run trend and carry forecasts together; dynamically give more weight to whichever has outperformed over trailing year, then smooth the weight.
cases.interpretation: Strategy-of-strategies allocation driven by relative sub-strategy performance.
cases.reason: strategy-as-block; dynamic module weighting; child-result input

cases.source: Use trend/carry forecasts but scale positions larger when current risk is below normal and smaller when risk is above normal.
cases.interpretation: Continuous regime-dependent position sizing based on relative risk level.

cases.source: Daily liquid large-cap universe; choose up to 10 highest 252d annualized Sharpe names above SMA200 and minimum Sharpe; equal weight at 1.5x gross; adaptive Kijun minus 4x ATR exit.
cases.interpretation: Fundamental/liquidity universe -> risk-adjusted rank -> trend gate -> leverage -> volatility-adjusted structural stop.
cases.reason: cross-sectional ranking; leverage; adaptive stop; schedule separation

cases.source: Open up to three new strong-trend names daily, but also add to existing holdings on pullbacks from 52-week highs when average price since the high is declining; max 15 holdings, 25% cash, profit exit + cooldowns.
cases.interpretation: Two distinct entry pathways (new momentum vs add-on pullback), shared portfolio caps, path-dependent metrics and cooldowns.
cases.reason: multiple entry modes; since-event metric; cooldown; portfolio cap

cases.source: Use limit orders normally, but market orders for urgent exits or extreme volatility when fill certainty matters more than price.
cases.interpretation: Execution method branches on urgency/volatility context.

cases.source: Use stop loss but no fixed take profit; trail winners so occasional large R multiples remain possible.
cases.interpretation: Exit policy combines hard downside stop with open-ended trailing profit management.

cases.source: Map different option structures to market/IV regimes: range -> strangles, tight range -> iron fly, trend -> verticals, panic -> tail hedges, etc.
cases.interpretation: Meta-strategy chooses child strategy based on regime classification.

cases.source: Some traders define the wheel as accepting assignment and cycling naturally; others roll positions under selected conditions.
cases.interpretation: Same named strategy has incompatible management semantics; rolling must be an explicit policy rather than implied by strategy name.

cases.source: Do not trade until the first 15-minute opening range is fully formed.
cases.interpretation: Lock the session opening range after 15 minutes; entries before formation are prohibited.

cases.source: After price breaks the opening range, do not chase; wait for price to come back to the broken boundary.
cases.interpretation: Breakout is only a precursor; a later retest is required before entry evaluation.
cases.fuzzy: break with conviction; do not chase
cases.reason: event sequence; state flag; structural level

cases.source: Only treat the retest as an entry when a candle holds the level and closes back in the breakout direction.
cases.interpretation: Retest must be followed by directional candle confirmation.

cases.source: If fakeouts are a concern, wait for a second confirming candle rather than the first.
cases.interpretation: Optional stricter confirmation requires two consecutive confirming bars.

cases.source: Use premarket and weekly highs/lows as secondary context around the opening-range setup.
cases.interpretation: Primary opening-range event is conditioned by levels derived from other session/time horizons.

cases.source: Place the stop just beyond the retest level rather than using an unrelated fixed percentage.
cases.interpretation: Risk boundary is derived from the structural retest level.

cases.source: Sell cash-secured puts only on companies you would be comfortable owning if assignment happens.
cases.interpretation: Underlying eligibility depends on a discretionary ownership-acceptance predicate.

cases.source: After put assignment, do not automatically sell a covered call; consider waiting for a rebound first.
cases.interpretation: Assignment changes strategy state; covered-call transition may be delayed by a rebound condition.

cases.source: A different rule is to wait for implied volatility to rebuild rather than waiting for price itself to rebound.
cases.interpretation: Post-assignment transition can be gated by IV recovery instead of price recovery.

cases.source: If selling the call immediately, choose a farther-OTM and shorter-DTE contract so the stock has room to recover.
cases.interpretation: Contract selection changes conditionally when the call is opened immediately after assignment.

cases.source: Use effective cost basis after put premium when deciding how low a covered-call strike can be.
cases.interpretation: Strike constraint depends on path-dependent cost basis, not just current price.

cases.source: Avoid repeatedly capping recovery at the worst entry price after assignment.
cases.interpretation: Covered-call strike policy depends on recovery state and prior entry economics.

cases.source: If assigned shares fall far below cost basis, one approach is to sell a weekly call around a target delta and repeat until called away.
cases.interpretation: Underwater assigned state triggers repeated short-DTE call cycle using delta-based strike selection.

cases.source: Another approach uses a longer-DTE call and rolls it up and out if the stock begins to recover toward the strike.
cases.interpretation: Recovery event can trigger a roll transition on an existing covered call.

cases.source: A more conservative branch uses a lower-delta call to chip away at cost basis gradually.
cases.interpretation: Underwater state selects lower-delta contract as a different recovery policy.

cases.source: A different branch is to stop writing calls temporarily and hold shares with a trailing stop until price recovers enough to resume calls.
cases.interpretation: Strategy can suspend one module, switch to hold/trailing-stop mode, then reactivate it after recovery.

cases.source: Sell cash-secured puts until assignment occurs.
cases.interpretation: Remain in short-put state and repeat expirations until assignment event.

cases.source: Once assigned, switch from selling puts to selling covered calls.
cases.interpretation: Assignment is a state transition that changes the active strategy module.

cases.source: Continue selling covered calls until shares are called away, then return to the put-selling state.
cases.interpretation: Call-away event closes the shares state and loops back to initial module.

cases.source: During a recession or large correction, consider pausing the wheel rather than applying normal rules unchanged.
cases.interpretation: Market-regime event can override the normal strategy loop and enter a paused mode.
cases.fuzzy: large correction; market forms a bottom

cases.source: One discretionary restart rule is to wait until the market appears to form a bottom and show strength before wheeling again.
cases.interpretation: Paused mode exits only after fuzzy bottom/strength confirmation.

cases.source: After crisis assignment, delay covered calls longer so the newly acquired shares have more recovery time.
cases.interpretation: Crisis context modifies the normal post-assignment transition timing.

cases.source: Only take one high-conviction trade per day rather than every available setup.
cases.interpretation: Daily state enforces a maximum of one accepted trade after a subjective conviction gate.

cases.source: Avoid the first 30 minutes because volatility is more likely to stop the trade out.
cases.interpretation: Session-time exclusion overrides otherwise valid entries.

cases.source: Use 9/21 EMA trend context plus support/resistance confirmation before taking the breakout.
cases.interpretation: Entry requires confluence of trend and structural-level context.

cases.source: Attach OCO orders with a large profit target and tight loss threshold immediately after entry.
cases.interpretation: Entry automatically creates mutually exclusive exit orders.

cases.source: Use only long calls or puts, one strike OTM, rather than switching to complex option structures.
cases.interpretation: Instrument/contract policy restricts expression to directional long options.

cases.source: Enter roughly 1.5 to 2 hours after the open rather than immediately.
cases.interpretation: Entry window is relative to session-open event.

cases.source: Skip days with major scheduled news such as FOMC or CPI even when technical conditions look valid.
cases.interpretation: Event calendar provides a global no-trade override.

cases.source: Choose the short strike using a target probability-of-profit or delta range, then choose a spread width.
cases.interpretation: Option structure selection is a sequence of contract constraints.

cases.source: Use a limit order near the bid/ask midpoint and explicitly avoid market orders.
cases.interpretation: Execution method is constrained by a price derived from current quote.

cases.source: Exit if loss reaches a multiple of collected premium or a percentage of max loss.
cases.interpretation: Stop can be expressed relative to trade-specific economics rather than price.

cases.source: Observe SPX/SPY direction during a morning window before deciding which side of the spread to sell.
cases.interpretation: A pre-entry observation window classifies morning direction and selects put-spread vs call-spread module.

cases.source: Place the short strike at a distance derived from a multiple of the current ATM straddle price.
cases.interpretation: Contract strike is calculated from another option-market observation.

cases.source: Avoid special high-risk geopolitical/event periods even if the mechanical setup otherwise qualifies.
cases.interpretation: External event context can override the core mechanical strategy.
cases.fuzzy: early stages of war; smart to avoid

cases.source: A variant only trades condors when SPX is above a moving average and VIX is below a threshold.
cases.interpretation: Directional/volatility regime filters gate an option-income module.

cases.source: One management policy holds the spread through expiration because early profit-taking reduced total P/L in backtests.
cases.interpretation: Exit policy is explicitly chosen from prior strategy-level evidence, not a fixed generic rule.

cases.source: Only enter when price is near a dealer gamma-flip zone; otherwise skip the trade entirely.
cases.interpretation: Entry requires proximity to an externally derived structural zone.

cases.source: Place the stop at the nearest major gamma wall instead of a fixed premium percentage.
cases.interpretation: Risk boundary is selected from external options-positioning structure.

cases.source: Check volatility risk premium before each session and skip the day when implied volatility is far above realized volatility.
cases.interpretation: Session-level external statistic creates a no-trade state.

cases.source: Do not buy merely because price touched support; wait for evidence that price is actually being rejected from the level.
cases.interpretation: Structural touch creates a pending setup, not an immediate entry.

cases.source: Whether a support touch matters depends on how price arrived there and what the higher timeframe is doing.
cases.interpretation: Same local event is interpreted differently based on path and higher-timeframe context.

cases.source: Look for volume to appear as price turns away from the level.
cases.interpretation: Rejection confirmation combines structural reversal with contemporaneous volume evidence.
cases.fuzzy: volume come in; turn price around

cases.source: Require multiple confirmations rather than treating support/resistance as a standalone signal.
cases.interpretation: A level is one feature in a configurable confluence rule.

cases.source: Use the higher timeframe to define oversold/context, then wait for a lower-timeframe trend shift to time the entry.
cases.interpretation: Higher timeframe supplies setup state; lower timeframe supplies transition event.

cases.source: If trading a 15-minute setup, look upward to 30-minute or 1-hour context rather than downward to 5-minute noise.
cases.interpretation: Context timeframe is constrained to a parent horizon relative to execution timeframe.

cases.source: News-driven or market-open moves are exceptions because lower-timeframe reversals can become aggressive before higher-timeframe confirmation.
cases.interpretation: Event type overrides the normal top-down confirmation sequence.

cases.source: Run a fast-profit and slow-profit version of the strategy in parallel as proxies for choppy and trending regimes.
cases.interpretation: Two child strategies execute simultaneously as regime sensors.

cases.source: Record each child strategy portfolio value every minute and resample it into 5-minute OHLC as if each strategy were an asset.
cases.interpretation: Strategy performance itself becomes a time series input to another model.

cases.source: Apply MACD to the two strategy-performance series to decide which strategy should be active.
cases.interpretation: Indicator over strategy-level performance selects active child module.

cases.source: The switching logic exists because one exit policy tends to close too early in trends and another too late in chop.
cases.interpretation: Meta-strategy is motivated by regime-dependent failure modes of child strategies.

cases.source: Keep separate strategies for different market types and let each activate only when its market is present.
cases.interpretation: Regime classifier routes control to different strategy modules.

cases.source: Use SPY direction or sideways chop as a market-wide regime input for otherwise separate strategies.
cases.interpretation: Parent market state controls child strategy eligibility.

cases.source: Build regime classification from longer timeframes and multiple sectors/markets rather than only the traded symbol.
cases.interpretation: Regime state aggregates multi-market and higher-timeframe features.

cases.source: A more complex version lets a model choose among hundreds of technical, fundamental and options-derived regime features.
cases.interpretation: Regime classifier consumes heterogeneous feature families before routing strategy behavior.

cases.source: Classify 15-minute, 1-hour and 4-hour NQ independently as bull, bear or neutral before combining them.
cases.interpretation: Each timeframe has its own state machine; the parent view aggregates states.

cases.source: Use DXY, multiple Treasury yields, ES, RTY, SOXX, gold, oil and USDJPY as macro context rather than trading inputs themselves.
cases.interpretation: Cross-asset observations are grouped into macro pressure dimensions.

cases.source: Combine timeframe state and macro pressure into a weighted danger score and named regime.
cases.interpretation: Multiple semantic modules feed a composite score and discrete state.

cases.source: When danger rises above one threshold reduce risk; above a higher threshold stop opening new positions.
cases.interpretation: Different score thresholds trigger graded actions rather than one Boolean entry.

cases.source: Use the regime tool as a position-sizing/circuit-breaker layer rather than as the entry signal itself.
cases.interpretation: Context module modifies downstream strategy without owning entries.

cases.source: Measure trend, momentum, structure, volume flow and mean-reversion on each of nine timeframes, then normalize them before combining.
cases.interpretation: Factor families are evaluated per timeframe and normalized into comparable scores.

cases.source: Change factor weights by regime so trend matters more in trends and mean-reversion matters more in ranges.
cases.interpretation: The weight of a signal is conditional on another classifier state.

cases.source: Also scale factor weights by how well each factor historically followed through on the current symbol.
cases.interpretation: Signal weight depends on symbol-specific trailing performance of that signal.

cases.source: If all signals align but the market is overextended, damp the confluence rather than treating alignment as maximum conviction.
cases.interpretation: Exhaustion is an exception that reduces an otherwise strong composite signal.

cases.source: Flag when fast timeframes turn against slow timeframes as a transition rather than forcing a single bullish/bearish label.
cases.interpretation: Cross-timeframe disagreement is represented as its own transitional state.

cases.source: Build a regime score from slope difference, line distance, neutral anchor, divergence and volume expansion.
cases.interpretation: Several heterogeneous observations contribute weighted points/bonuses to a score.

cases.source: Do not flip regime immediately when the score crosses a threshold; require it to remain beyond the threshold for several bars.
cases.interpretation: Threshold crossing creates a pending state that must persist for N bars.

cases.source: After a regime shift, enforce a minimum number of bars before another shift can occur.
cases.interpretation: Cooldown prevents rapid state oscillation after transition.

cases.source: Treat regime-shift markers as context rather than direct entries.
cases.interpretation: State-change event informs downstream strategy but does not itself trade.

cases.source: Separate market-regime classification, directional evidence score and actual entry trigger instead of treating them as the same output.
cases.interpretation: Three semantic layers produce context, bias and event trigger separately.

cases.source: A bullish dashboard verdict does not automatically mean a long entry exists.
cases.interpretation: Context state must pass an additional trigger contract before action.

cases.source: Use confirmed divergence, volume evidence, macro relationships and momentum changes as separate evidence families in the directional score.
cases.interpretation: Composite score accepts heterogeneous evidence families.

cases.source: Classify the market into trend bull, trend bear, volatile bull, volatile bear, high-vol range, low-vol range or flat rather than only bull/bear.
cases.interpretation: Regime is a multi-state categorical variable.

cases.source: Warn about regime transitions before treating the new state as fully established.
cases.interpretation: Transition is represented as a distinct intermediate state.

cases.source: Use multi-timeframe alignment as part of confidence in the regime classification.
cases.interpretation: Confidence is a derived value from agreement across horizons.

cases.source: Use a volatility-aware Chandelier-style stop after regime/entry logic rather than a fixed stop.
cases.interpretation: Risk module consumes current volatility and position state after upstream context.

cases.source: Run trend and carry as separate forecast strategies and give more weight to whichever has outperformed over the trailing year.
cases.interpretation: Child-strategy relative performance controls their parent allocation weights.

cases.source: When trend and carry have performed equally, give them equal weight; positive relative performance tilts toward trend and negative tilts toward carry.
cases.interpretation: Signed relative-performance state maps continuously to module weights.

cases.source: Smooth the changing strategy weights so the allocation does not jump abruptly day to day.
cases.interpretation: Meta-allocation is passed through a temporal smoother before execution.

cases.source: Track theoretical holdings/performance for both child strategies even while only the combined parent portfolio is traded.
cases.interpretation: Counterfactual child states are maintained for meta-decision making.

cases.source: Increase position size when current risk is below normal and reduce it when risk is above normal.
cases.interpretation: Risk regime multiplicatively modifies downstream forecast sizing.

cases.source: Aggregate several trend forecasts and several carry forecasts before mixing the two families.
cases.interpretation: Nested aggregation first combines variants within each factor family, then combines families.

cases.source: Apply a diversification multiplier and cap the final forecast after factor aggregation.
cases.interpretation: Post-composition transform rescales and clips the parent signal.

cases.source: At the beginning of each month, compute unexpected earnings using current quarterly EPS versus EPS four quarters earlier.
cases.interpretation: Monthly event computes a feature relative to an event-aligned historical quarter.

cases.source: Standardize the earnings surprise by the historical variability of the same year-over-year EPS changes.
cases.interpretation: Current event surprise is normalized by a rolling distribution of prior comparable events.

cases.source: Rank the liquid universe by standardized surprise and hold the top five percent.
cases.interpretation: Event-derived cross-sectional score feeds percentile selection.

cases.source: Rank every stock separately on value, quality and momentum before combining those ranks.
cases.interpretation: Multiple cross-sectional ranks are first-class intermediate results.

cases.source: Use operating margin as quality, book value per share as value and recent return as momentum, then apply factor weights.
cases.interpretation: Heterogeneous factor semantics are normalized through rank before weighted combination.

cases.source: Go long the top-ranked stocks and short the bottom-ranked stocks at the same rebalance.
cases.interpretation: One ranking drives symmetric selection branches.

cases.source: Drop stocks with missing or zero factor values before ranking them.
cases.interpretation: Data-quality condition is a prerequisite to cross-sectional ranking.

cases.source: For each factor, place stocks into quintiles and convert quintile membership into a score.
cases.interpretation: Cross-sectional bucket membership is transformed into ordinal points.

cases.source: Average or equally combine factor scores, rerank the composite, then select the top 20.
cases.interpretation: Nested rank-score-rank pipeline constructs the final selection.

cases.source: Repeat the whole ranking process each month rather than keeping membership static.
cases.interpretation: Dynamic group membership is recomputed on schedule.

cases.source: First select liquid stocks above a minimum price, then run PCA only on that reduced universe.
cases.interpretation: Model stage depends on an upstream liquidity/price universe filter.

cases.source: Use principal components as common factors, regress each stock on them, then trade residual deviations rather than raw price deviations.
cases.interpretation: Derived latent factors feed per-asset residual models before signal generation.

cases.source: Only select stocks whose residual z-score is sufficiently negative for the mean-reversion long basket.
cases.interpretation: Model residual state is filtered by a standardized threshold.

cases.source: Weight selected positions using the magnitude of residual deviations rather than equal weight.
cases.interpretation: Portfolio sizing is a function of signal magnitude.

cases.source: Use a one-year formation period to decide which stocks historically moved together before any pair trade exists.
cases.interpretation: Pair identity itself is dynamically learned from a historical formation window.

cases.source: Normalize price series before measuring which partner minimizes squared divergence.
cases.interpretation: Relationship selection uses transformed relative price paths rather than raw prices.

cases.source: Only after a selected pair diverges sufficiently do you open opposite long/short positions expecting convergence.
cases.interpretation: Pair selection and trade trigger are separate stages.

cases.source: Rank country ETFs by trailing 36-month return, buy the worst four and short the best four.
cases.interpretation: Long-horizon cross-sectional contrarian ranking creates both portfolio tails.

cases.source: Rebalance only every three years even though a monthly scheduled event checks whether it is time.
cases.interpretation: Frequent scheduler contains a state counter that suppresses action until a long interval has elapsed.

cases.source: Treat stocks more than one standard deviation below their 30-day mean as candidates for mean reversion.
cases.interpretation: Current price is standardized against its own rolling distribution.

cases.source: Apply the rule only to a preselected basket rather than the whole market.
cases.interpretation: Mean-reversion logic consumes an externally defined target set.

cases.source: Compute the average daily high-low range over 25 days before deriving the entry band.
cases.interpretation: A rolling volatility-like statistic is an upstream dependency of the band.

cases.source: Define the lower band from the 10-day rolling high minus 2.5 times the average high-low range.
cases.interpretation: Entry boundary composes two differently windowed statistics.

cases.source: Go long only when price closes below that band and IBS is below 0.3.
cases.interpretation: Entry requires both structural deviation and intrabar-position confirmation.

cases.source: Exit when the close rises above the previous day high.
cases.interpretation: Exit is relative to a prior-event structural level rather than entry price.

cases.source: At each monthly rebalance, predict next-month returns for a set of risk-on and risk-off assets.
cases.interpretation: Scheduled model inference produces per-asset forward scores.

cases.source: Allocate only to assets with positive predicted returns.
cases.interpretation: Prediction sign gates portfolio eligibility.

cases.source: Scale each selected position by the magnitude of its predicted return.
cases.interpretation: Model score controls allocation size, not only selection.

cases.source: When one side of an iron condor is challenged, roll the untested spread inward to collect more premium.
cases.interpretation: Which leg group to adjust depends on current tested/untested state.

cases.source: Move the entire untested vertical spread together rather than changing a single leg in isolation.
cases.interpretation: Adjustment operation preserves the internal relation of a multi-leg module.

cases.source: If the market outlook changes enough that the iron condor no longer expresses the thesis, close it and choose a new structure rather than endlessly adjusting it.
cases.interpretation: A thesis-state change can terminate the current strategy module and replace it.

cases.source: A lighter adjustment is to roll the untested side up or up-and-out while leaving the tested side in place.
cases.interpretation: Adjustment targets one submodule based on tested-state classification.

cases.source: If the goal is to harvest earnings IV crush, open the short-volatility structure close to the earnings event rather than too early.
cases.interpretation: Trade timing is defined relative to a scheduled corporate event.

cases.source: Opening too early can expose the position to the pre-earnings volatility run-up before the intended crush occurs.
cases.interpretation: Pre-event phase is a distinct risk state that can invalidate an otherwise correct thesis.

cases.source: If strongly bullish on the underlying, consider fewer calls, farther strikes or longer expiries so premium income does not cap too much upside.
cases.interpretation: Covered-call contract selection depends on the investor thesis and desired assignment probability.
cases.fuzzy: strongly bullish; low risk of assignment

cases.source: The choice between more contracts farther out and fewer contracts closer in is a tradeoff between premium and assignment risk.
cases.interpretation: Coverage ratio, strike distance and DTE are jointly constrained variables rather than independent knobs.
cases.fuzzy: small but consistent premium; low risk

cases.source: Screen for cheap stocks with very high volume and high implied volatility before selling cash-secured puts.
cases.interpretation: Option strategy starts with a multi-factor underlying eligibility screen.
cases.fuzzy: volume jumped exponentially; something big happened

cases.source: Prefer names where volume has increased roughly two to three times because that is interpreted as evidence of a major event.
cases.interpretation: Relative-volume surge is used as a fuzzy proxy for latent company event/state.
cases.fuzzy: something big happened or will happen

cases.source: Choose roughly 40-day expiries and a strike near current price, then buy back after most of the premium has decayed.
cases.interpretation: Entry contract and exit profit are linked to an intended theta-decay cycle.

cases.source: If assigned early, average down using premium and switch to a covered call whose premium compensates for selling below average cost.
cases.interpretation: Assignment triggers a recovery branch using path-dependent cost basis and premium constraint.
cases.fuzzy: boring part; rather make small gain than large loss
